stories.notes: Empty acceptance criteria and no existing spec — story needs full requirements elaboration before hardening. Cross-platform (GO, UP, MX) live preview is complex and high-risk: openspec must refine AC and propose technical depth first, then speckit adds testability, security, and edge-case coverage. No prior hand-curation detected.

agentContributions.notes: Novel story — Live Preview of Content in CMS does not exist in the codebase. The central attachment point is useContent, which 236+ components call via getContentByKey. Live Preview must integrate there to propagate real-time content updates to all consumers without modifying each component. Contentstack.io is unreachable at test time, so VCs are written to the boundary of our code.

Openspec provided empty acceptance criteria with a valuable architectural note about useContent/getContentByKey (236+ consumers) and ContentstackContext as the integration point. I generated all 16 criteria from scratch based on the story title, file paths, and openspec's architectural note. I could NOT read the four listed files (src/hooks/useContent.ts, src/context/ContentstackContext.tsx, src/interface/content/contentCard.ts, src/components/contentstack/ContentstackLink/ContentstackLink.tsx), so these criteria are based on reasonable assumptions about their roles. Criteria may need adjustment once file contents are visible — particularly AC-10 (nested contentCard fields) and AC-16 (type compatibility). I included AC-9 to ensure live-preview does not activate outside the CMS preview environment, which is a common pitfall. AC-11/AC-12 cover security. AC-13 covers accessibility. AC-14 covers rapid-event debouncing. AC-15 covers resource cleanup.

coordinatorReview.reviewNotes: Both agents added meaningful, non-overlapping value: openspec identified the novel story, pinpointed useContent/getContentByKey (236+ consumers) as the central integration point, and flagged ContentstackContext as the boundary — valuable architectural context that speckit then built upon. Speckit generated 16 acceptance criteria from scratch covering testability, security (AC-11/12), accessibility (AC-13), debouncing (AC-14), and resource cleanup (AC-15). No redundancy between the two contributions. However, speckit explicitly could not read the four listed source files (useContent.ts, ContentstackContext.tsx, contentCard.ts, ContentstackLink.tsx), meaning all 16 criteria are based on assumptions about file structure and roles. This is a significant gap — criteria may not align with actual code, particularly AC-10 (nested contentCard fields) and AC-16 (type compatibility). Human review is required to verify criteria against the real source files before implementation begins.
